transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for taking the time to review the draft student council election plan. As you know, the election is scheduled for the last school day of the month, and the current draft includes an online ballot, a candidate forum during lunch, and publication of vote totals at the end of election day. Before I give my final approval, I'd like to hear from each of you — counselor, technology coordinator, and family liaison — about any concerns or suggestions you have. Please go ahead and share your thoughts.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to raise an urgent concern. I tested the draft online ballot this morning and found that the platform records each voter's identity for 90 days, and that feature cannot be disabled. This creates a privacy issue for our student voters. The approved workaround is to use sealed paper ballots counted by two adults, which would create zero electronic voter records. I have not yet updated the election plan to reflect this change, so the draft you're reviewing still references the online ballot.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to raise a serious concern. I conducted a confidential student-safety review and found a substantiated retaliation concern involving two students in this election. Because of this, our student-privacy protocol requires anonymous voting and prohibits releasing vote totals until the election is certified. I've kept the review in my counseling file since it contains protected student information, and I have not yet briefed you on it. This means the current draft plan's publication of vote totals at the end of election day would violate our privacy protocol, and the voting method must ensure complete anonymity.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to raise an important concern regarding language access. During this week's family outreach, I confirmed with families that election instructions, ballots, and candidate statements are needed in English, Spanish, and Arabic. The translation request is still pending with the communications office, but the draft plan currently lists only English materials. This needs to be incorporated into the plan before approval to ensure all our families can participate.

I want to note that my language access concern and your privacy and technology concerns all need to be addressed together in the revised plan. If we're moving to paper ballots as Mr. Shah suggested, we'll need printed ballots in all three languages — English, Spanish, and Arabic — and the candidate statements and instructions will also need to be translated and available at the forum.
